summary: Make governed artifact identity stable across Git line-ending conversion while binding dirty and untracked files to their actual Git-canonical content.
reason: The execution-gate target-state calculation is a completion control. Raw working-tree byte hashing made the same committed Git content acquire different identities after checkout line-ending conversion. The correction hashes the actual governed file through Git's path-aware clean/EOL filters, preserves deterministic ABSENT state, keeps repository-containment checks, fails closed when Git identity cannot be established, and does not rewrite historical review evidence.

reasons: The correction is bounded to one artifact-state identity function and its direct regression tests.

The Adversarial review can evaluate the material failure surfaces—checkout normalization, dirty/untracked content binding, path containment, fail-closed Git errors, absent paths, and stale-credit risk—in one separated pass.

workload.notes: SEPARATED default; no FUSED permission requested and no subdivision required.

capability.benchmark_evidence: Built-in separated default; not a claim of measured reviewer capability.

decision.assurance_boundary: Semantic judgment determines whether one pass is suitable and which bounded subpasses require isolation. Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. The gate and completion validator enforce the recorded plan but do not prove the semantic assessment itself was correct.
